page.layout: One page of running text, a single column. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. One marginal note in the left margin, "Luc. 9.", beside the line "aduersum nos". Nothing below the text. Show-through and edge marks at the right edge are left out.

main_text.l: etiam in ea degentia secundùm formam exter-
nam & ordinem aspectabilem illius; illi verò
amici, quamuis extra Ecclesiam positi, qui nec
oderunt Ecclesiam animo, nec sermone aut fa-
cto obsunt; sed aut bene cupiunt ipsi ex animo,
quamuis ipsi sibi id non cupiant boni, aut certè
amicè ferunt, vt Ecclesia sit, atq. tranquilla sit:
de quo genere dicebat Christus, Qui non est
aduersum nos, pro nobis est. Pro his ergo om-
nibus Ecclesia postulat, vt ipsis bene sit, & tran-
quillitate fruantur, denique communibus
se-cum beneficiis magis ac magis cumulentur
à Domino.
Alterum verò optatum in versu 7. quod ad
domesticos Ecclesiæ pertinet, duas partes illas
pacis evidenter notat, de quibus antè diceba-
mus in definienda pace. Ad iustam enim & ve-
ram pacem desiderantur duo: defensio à malo,
& bonorum pacis perceptio. De utroque pre-
ces concipiendas oftendit Psaltes verbis paucis-
simis; & feruata typi illius, qui tum ad figuran-
dam Ecclesiam fuerat datus, allegoria. Ierusa-
lem typus erat Ecclesiæ: ad tranquillitatem vr-
bis illius duo hæc fuerunt opus, tum vt aduer-
sus mala foris minantia & irruentia circummu-
nita esset vrbs, tum vt intus abundaret bonis.
Defensionem à malo Propheta his verbis docuit
expetendam; Sit pax in præmunitione tua: Con-
stitutionem verò stabilem in bono ac floren-
tissimam postulare docuit illis; Sit tranquillitas

page.notes: Running head "EIRENICES" is read from the spaced capitals and is uncertain. "Psaltes" was read as Psaltes, "pacis" and "paucis-simis" as printed; the hyphenated line breaks are kept as printed. Two lines ending in printed hyphens ("diceba-mus", "figuran-dam") were joined only where the hyphen is printed. The final line ends in a printed hyphen, so the text continues on the next page.
